answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with unique bandwidth proofs. Each identity must prove it controls a distinct, attested network pipe, and the network rejects identities that share one pipe. A farm behind a single connection cannot mint many identities, because they would all report the same pipe. Like timber from one orchard, each identity is cut from its own source, and like a sonnet, the pipe carries only one voice at a time. Each extra fake needs its own distinct network pipe with its own bandwidth allocation, a cost that cannot be shared, parallelized, or bought in bulk.
